hook_text: In the early 1800s, the most powerful people on the northern frontier weren't the British. They were the Kora and Griqua.
clip_script: The Kora: Khoikhoi herders pushed north to the Orange River, now on horseback with guns. The Griqua: people of mixed descent, denied land in the colony, who built their own captaincies, with laws and even coins, at Griquatown. Together they ran the trade between two worlds. Wagons and pack oxen carried guns, cloth, beads and tobacco north into the interior. They came back loaded with ivory, cattle, skins and ostrich feathers. Controlling guns and horses made them powerful, until diamonds were found and Britain took Griqua land in 1871.
visual_style: A wide river at sunset; wagons and pack oxen crossing a drift; close-ups of beads, tobacco rolls and an ivory tusk being exchanged.
pacing: Two introductions, a trade montage, a sharp ending.
